Egoroff's theorem bridges pointwise a.e. convergence to uniform convergence on large subsets, crucial for statistical learning theory. Its converse fails when measure is infinite, leading to non-uniform convergence counter-examples. Uniform essential boundedness ensures stability under composition, while approximate Borel measurability handles practical measurement noise. These four primitives form a minimal axiom set for verifying ergodicity and uniform convergence in predictive models.
